problem: The points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(0,-3)$ and $(4,-5)$, respectively, and the segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ is a diameter of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.

feedback.worked_solution:
The diameter can be calculated using the distance formula: 

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3-9)^{2}+(-4-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-12)^{2}+(-12)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144+144} \\  & =\sqrt{288} \\  & =12\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is half the diameter:

$$
r=\frac{d}{2}=\frac{12\sqrt{2}}{2}=6\sqrt{2}
$$
